scope: Where the expert formal model (formal/) departs from the source documents. Only the formal model and the documents are compared; results/, claims/ and flow/ are not part of this file. Entries marked material=false were found in passing; the minor list is not exhaustive.

categories.contradiction: The formal model does something the documents rule out.
categories.convention: The formal model fixes a choice the documents leave open or do not state.
categories.scope: The formal model contains content that is not in the documents.

doc_check.confirmed: The quoted text was checked in the document, or the document was searched and is silent on the point.
doc_check.pending: Not yet confirmed against the whole document set.

document.quote: An attacker can create an account at a legitimate client and initiate the authorization flow.

entries.description: At the authorization endpoint the server talks only to the UserAgent process, over TLS channels handed out on a private channel the attacker never obtains, so only honest user agents can send an authorization request; there is no resource-owner process and no resource-owner authentication. TLS protects only the request direction: the authorization response goes out on the public net. The document treats the attacker as a party that can start authorization flows and requires the server to verify the resource owner's identity.

document.quote: Before initiating the protocol, the client registers with the authorization server.

entries.description: Only one honest client (A) is registered and run; B is declared but unused, and the attacker cannot reach the token endpoint, so no attacker-registered client exists. The document places no limit on which clients register.

document.quote: A refresh token is a string representing the authorization granted to the client by the resource owner.

entries.description: On the refresh path the server fetches an arbitrary authorization code issued to the client; the refresh-token table does not record which grant the refresh token came from, so a refreshed token is not bound to its originating authorization.

document.quote: The HTTP request method in upper case.

entries.description: The MAC input is (nonce, URI) only; the document's normalized request string has seven elements (nonce, method, request-URI, host, port, body hash, ext).

document.quote: Ensure that the combination of nonce and MAC key identifier received from the client has not been used before

entries.description: The resource server never checks the nonce for replay.

document.quote: If an authorization code is used more than once, the authorization server MUST deny the request

entries.description: Authorization codes are looked up but never marked as used, so a code can be redeemed more than once.
